transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST | Duration: 38m | Meeting ID: ff-20260304-verdigris-8421
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Verdigris - Head of Search), Oliver Park (Verdigris - ML Eng), Sam Rodriguez (Verdigris - CTO)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery to map architecture and define pilot metrics.

00:00 Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, and with me is Arjun our solutions engineer. quick round of intros?
00:08 Maya: Hi this is Maya, head of search at Verdigris. We're evaluating options for embeddings-based reranking for our product search.
00:14 Oliver: Oliver here, I run the ML infra side, so I care about throughput and cost.
00:19 Sam: Sam, CTO, looking at security and long-term ops.
00:23 Arjun: Great, thanks. Can you give us a sense of your current stack and where embeddings live today?
00:30 Maya: Sure. Right now we generate 1536-dim embeddings using a hosted model - we use an external API and store vectors in Pinecone, mostly using kNN for candidate retrieval then a small transformer for rerank. Latency is... kind of a problem at scale. p95 on search is around 350ms when combined.
00:49 Lena: And what's your QPS now and target?
00:52 Oliver: We're running about 40 qps peak during certain campaign windows; steady is more like 8-12 qps. For pilot we want to hit 100 QPS on dedicated infra eventually, but realistic first target is 50 QPS with p95 under 200ms end-to-end for the rerank flow.
01:08 Arjun: Helpful. Is vector store only Pinecone or do you run FAISS/Weaviate in-house for some partitions?
01:15 Maya: Currently Pinecone for production; we do some offline FAISS runs for reindexing. We're evaluating moving some hot shards into a dedicated infra or even private deployment because of data residency concerns.
01:27 Lena: Got it. A few common tradeoffs we see: hosted makes it fastest to get started — low operational work — but dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost per token, private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance. Curious if you have SOC2/ISO requirements?
01:43 Sam: We do need SOC 2 and ISO 27001 for some enterprise clients; also need KMS integration and SSO.
01:50 Arjun: Redwood supports SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integrations in Private mode, and Dedicated can be provisioned in a VPC as well. For audits we surface audit logs via the Console.
01:59 Maya: Nice — how does the rerank pipeline look with Redwood? Are we talking streaming tokens or whole response? How do you handle prefix caching and kv cache?
02:10 Arjun: We do token streaming for certain models but for rerank we usually run short scoring calls. Our runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching so repeated context across requests can be cached; we call it KV cache but sometimes the autop transcribes as kv cash, so ignore that.
02:26 Oliver: Question on dimensionality: we use 1536 embeddings now. If Redwood recommends 768 dim model for cost, what's the perf hit?
02:34 Arjun: There's a tradeoff — 768-dim models reduce storage and compute costs roughly ~2x depending on hardware and quantization. Accuracy depends on your dataset; sometimes fine-tuning or hybrid search (keywords + vector) recovers any small drop. We recommend benchmarking both.
02:50 Maya: Hybrid search is important for us — we need exact term matches for brand SKUs plus semantic for longtail. Does Redwood support hybrid search natively or is that on the vector DB side?
02:59 Arjun: Redwood returns embeddings and can do rerank scoring; for hybrid we typically combine a vector candidate set from your DB (Pinecone/Weaviate/FAISS) with a lexical filter and then run a lightweight reranker in Redwood to merge scores. We also have suggestions for index-time metadata to speed filters.
03:18 Sam: If we go Dedicated, can we pin model versions? We don't want it changing mid-pilot.
03:22 Lena: Yes, you can pin model versions and use rollout policies for canary tests; Dedicated and Private both support pinning and A/B rollouts.
03:30 Oliver: Throughput question — for 50 QPS at p95 < 200ms, what kind of nodes? GPUs? Any rough cost?
03:37 Arjun: For short scoring calls with 1536-dim embedding model and a mid-size transformer reranker, typical dedicated setup is 2-4 A100-ish GPUs for 50-100 qps depending on batching. With quantization and optimized kernels we can squeeze more. We'll include an estimated cost sheet in the pilot proposal.
03:56 Maya: We're also concerned about vector DB integration. We use Pinecone today; is that a first-class integration? How do you handle consistency between Redwood reranker and vector DB?
04:06 Arjun: Pinecone is first-class — we have guides and a connector pattern. Typical flow: your search service asks Pinecone for top-N, then sends candidates + query to Redwood for rerank scoring. We recommend returning a score vector so you can combine with Pinecone's scoring and apply your business rules. If you want to migrate to a Dedicated/private hosted Weaviate/FAISS, we have docs for that too.
04:29 Oliver: Any recommended top-N for rerank? We're doing top-100 today which is heavy.
04:33 Arjun: Top-N can usually be reduced to 20-50 for rerank if your retrieval quality is good. We also support late interaction and cross-encoder style rerankers that can work on smaller sets more accurately. We'll benchmark top-20, 50 vs 100 for your dataset.
04:49 Maya: What's the pilot look like? We want realistic numbers: QPS, cold start, warm cache, hit rates.
04:55 Lena: Typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 0-1 onboarding and data ingest, week 2 run benchmarks (latency, throughput, quality), week 3 quality tuning and hybrid config, week 4 wrap and decision. We'll propose dedicated nodes for pilot but can start hosted to validate correctness.
05:12 Sam: Security — for S3 access to ship vectors we need temporary creds and an NDA.
05:17 Lena: We can accept a pre-signed S3 link or a read-only role; we'll also send our SOC2 and security pack after the call.
05:22 Oliver: For metrics, can you track token-level cost and per-route breakdowns?
05:26 Arjun: Yes Console shows per-request token breakdown, latency histograms, and cost by model/route. We can also add custom tracing hooks.
05:34 Maya: Any gotchas with quantized models and rerank accuracy? We saw some flakiness in past when using 4-bit quantized encoders.
05:41 Arjun: Quantization can affect final scores; usually a 4-bit quantized encoder for retrieval is fine, but for final cross-encoder reranker we often keep FP16 or 8-bit to preserve accuracy. We'll run A/B on quantization profiles.
05:54 Maya: Who owns the evaluation? Do you run it or do we?
05:57 Lena: Collaborative — we provide the benchmark harness and sample scripts; you run it against your data or we can run it in a secure pilot account. For private deployments we can run tests in your VPC.
06:08 Oliver: About logging — need audit logs accessible and retention policy configurable.
06:12 Arjun: Console exports audit logs and you can set retention in Private deployments. Dedicated includes extended retention as an addon.
06:19 Maya: Competitive question — how are you different vs Pinecone?
06:22 Lena: Pinecone is a vector DB; Redwood is the inference layer + orchestration. We play well with Pinecone but offer the rerank, model lifecycle, pinning, batching, and routing across hosted/dedicated/private. Think of Redwood as the scoring and serving platform, not just storage.
06:39 Sam: Ok makes sense. One more — latency SLOs during regional outages, do you have fallbacks?
06:45 Arjun: Yes smart routing — requests can route to another region or fallback to a cheaper model variant; there's automatic model variant fallback if capacity constrained. We'll show the routing policy config in the next demo.
06:57 Maya: Any reference customers doing exactly this flow?
07:00 Lena: We recently did a pilot with a retail search company — they used Pinecone + Redwood rerank and cut p95 by 45% while lowering per-query cost by 20 after batching and KV caching. We'll share that case study link.
07:12 Oliver: Great. For the sample data — we'll upload a 500 query sample and embed batch to an S3 presigned link.
07:18 Lena: Perfect. We'll follow up with pricing and pilot plan.
07:22 Sam: Thanks folks.
